angle: DL/EDGE: Run-the-Hoop lateral force (Hoop G) as a tiebreak lead for linemen who skip the 3-cone, with the pass-rush drill's get-off burst as the contrast (it carries into in-game first-second distance but not pressure); year-standardized; baseline = pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS score + official 10-yd split and 3-cone, fit leave-one-class-out
metric_name: Hoop G: peak half-second sideways acceleration (g) on the Run-the-Hoop curve, z within Combine year, shrunk for one-run reliability 0.41; plus call = 80% interval above zero
headline_number: Frozen plus calls beat the out-of-class no-tracking forecast 4 of 9 vs 9 of 69 (class-stratified exact mid-p 0.04; shuffle p 0.05; by class 1/3, 3/4, 0/2); plus calls lead in 18 of 27 sensitivity settings; count model with exposure, rotation and pick x rotation: 1.1 pressures per 450 rushes per sd [0.0, 2.5]; 3-cone held-out rho 0.36 [-0.22, 0.67].
what_changed_from_previous: Football: Hoop G stated as an empirical correlate with no in-game mechanism (two nulls with n), contrasted with the pass-rush drill's burst that does carry into games (rho 0.32, n 85) but not pressure; new 'When the call is wrong' case table (Johnson hit, Adebawore miss, Phillips vs Black minus flags) with alignment share, in-game get-off, and the cost of a wrong tie-break in pressures and EPA; 2025 card with a plain 'Action now' column instead of 'within noise'; jargon (twin, ghost alignment, T-E/E-T) removed; why the 3-cone should relate to pressure added. DS: per-class hit rates with Fisher and class-stratified exact mid-p; 27-cell sensitivity grid (call interval x minimum rushes x forecast spec) with a shuffle p per cell; 43 vs 45 3-cone counts reconciled (official vs tracked) in a footnote; the 27-rusher partial rho replaced by the 3-cone in the Bayesian count model (37 rushers) with class-alone signs and a held-out forecast-only ridge comparison; Hoop G count model refit with log rushes (exposure), rushes per game (rotation) and pick x rotation, split 100+ vs 30-99 rushes; simulated power for the 2026 prospective test (30% alone, 81% after four classes, 37% if the gap is half). Writeup: 75-word numeric lede ending 'A lead, not a rule'; 'How sure' cut to 4 rows with verdicts, technical rows moved to an appendix table. Viz: Fig 1 redrawn on the 'minus forecast, pp' axis with one colour key and the sampled-rush count; old Fig 2 split into a pairs figure with per-pair 90% intervals, 2025 marked hollow, mean and shuffle-null row, plus a new sensitivity-grid figure and a new held-out calibration plot.
open_risks: Evidence stays weak: stratified mid-p 0.04 and shuffle p 0.05 on 9 plus calls; the 2025 class goes 0 of 2 and cannot discriminate; best-of-14 screening p 0.12 is still the honest multiplicity price.

The 3-cone lead is barely supported once modelled as counts: 0.5 pressures per 450 rushes per sd [-1.0, 2.1], and adding it to a forecast-only ridge cut held-out error in only 1 of 3 classes; judges may ask why the lede still calls it the time most tied to pressure.

The sensitivity grid shows the edge disappears at a 90% call interval (only 1-2 calls), so the result depends on making enough calls; the forecast spec never changes a hit, which could read as the forecast variants being too similar.
The comparison-player (pairs) test and the case studies were designed after the rule was frozen, on the same rushers.
Rotation is proxied by rushes per game (no team snap counts); alignment context is lined-up position share only, so scheme claims remain film questions.
